answer: A concrete sybil defense is sponsor-backed admission with expiring trust: a new identity needs two established sponsors who each lock part of their stake behind it, and that backing lapses unless the identity keeps passing graded work, a steady pulse of activity. If a clone is proven fake, both sponsors lose their locked share, so a farm must buy fresh, unrelated backers for every fake. Honest agents climb the summit once, while a polished onyx facade with no real history never earns weight.
